Actually, many mods (think Requiem for Skyrim) make lockpicking more of an RPG mechanic and as a result it significantly detracts from the experience. Requiem in particular also trivializes combat by making it a matter of pure power-creep and character sheets rather than placement and skill, and again that detracts from the experience. Been there, done that. If you want a RPG that bad, I'd say pen and paper plus friends is a vastly better medium.

The construction of the TES games is incompatible with such pure RPG mechanics because they take control away from the player in an environment where the player has much finer control over what the PC does than your average RPG. The exact same issue was present with Morrowind's hit chance mechanic. It makes no sense to have such a model of hit chances when it's obvious the player is hitting the enemy physically. In my opinion the series would be better off by trashing much of the power-creeping aspect of its leveling system and concentrating on quests and choices.

You're right in that there is a balance to be found there.
